title: 無機・エネルギー機能化学
subtitle: Functional Chemistry of Inorganic and Energetic Materials
educationalGoal:
Students will learn:
(1) the classification of inorganic materials (ceramics, glasses, and metals).
(2) the properties and applications of inorganic materials in the fields of electronics, magnetics, and optics.
(3) about crystallography and the electronic structure of inorganic solids.
(4) about advanced functional materials and their practical applications.
advice:
This is an introductory course for materials science. The course will cover:
1. Substances and materials
2. Functions of inorganic materials
3. Crystal structures of solids
4. Electronic structures of solids
5. Preparation of functional materials
6. Optical and photonic properties of inorganic materials
7. Properties and production processes of glass
8. Dielectric materials, magnetic materials, and ion conducting oxides

Students must a scientific calculator or personal computer to every class.
Students should check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class.
books:
Textbooks: not specified
Reference books:"Nyu-mon Mukizairyou", Jiro Shiokawa, Kagaku Doujin (1997). ("Introduction to Inorganic Materials")
Reserved books: not specified
requiredKnowledge:
Basic knowledge of inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, and structural chemistry.
Refer to the basic concepts in textbooks such as Elements of Physical Chemistry by Atkins and Paula and to the  procedure for powder X-ray crystallography in Major Experimental Course B.

activityGoals.body: Be able to describe the crystal structure of typical inorganic materials
Be able to explain the electronic states of metals, semiconductors, and insulators and their electric properties
Be able to explain the functions of inorganic materials
Be able to explain the application of inorganic materials in the energy industry
Be able to describe methods for the production of inorganic materials

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Explain the concepts of crystal structure, bonding,  electronic structures, and their contribution to the electronic, magnetic, and optical functions of materials.
(2) Explain the processing of inorganic materials and their functions.
(3) Describe the applications of functional materials used in the research.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Explain the basic concepts of crystal structure, bonding,  and electronic structure.
(2) Explain the processing of inorganic materials and their functions.
(3) Describe the applications of functional materials used in the laboratory experiments.
